title: Two grounds: cause of all; uncaused from Himself
source_text: V. Haec autem summa naturae divinae perfectio colligitur ex duobus. 1. Ex eo quod Deus est rerum omnium causa. 2. Ex eo quod Deus nullam causam habet, sed per se est, & a seipso.
pass_a_gloss: But this highest perfection of the divine nature is gathered from two things. 1. From this that God is the cause of all things. 2. From this that God has no cause, but is through Himself, and from Himself.
pass_b_english: Highest divine perfection from two grounds.
He has no cause — through Himself, from Himself.

lemmas.gloss: is through Himself, and from Himself

choices.term: Deus nullam causam habet, sed per se est, & a seipso
choices.english: God has no cause, but is through Himself, and from Himself
rejected: God's perfection needs an external cause
